tagline: Across James Island to where the war began.
intro: Fort Johnson Road leaves Folly Road and runs four and a half miles across James Island toward its northeast point, where it passes a state gate and ends among the laboratories of the Marine Resources Center beside Charleston Harbor. New billboards are barred along it, and no tree thicker than six inches in the right-of-way may come down without the state's permission.

The island has seen its share of trouble. Tadeusz Kościuszko was nearly killed here in 1782, in the last known armed action of the Revolutionary War, and the Battle of Secessionville was fought here in the next war.

moments.title: James Island
moments.text: The island's town has been incorporated four times, the City of Charleston having taken the first three to court and won.

moments.title: Fort Johnson
moments.text: The road ends on the old ground of Fort Johnson, where the first shots of the Civil War were fired, now a 78-acre marine research campus beside the harbor.
